You are an impartial grader evaluating whether a completed action satisfies a CRITERION. You will be given:
  - The VALUE extracted from a tool call or agent output (as JSON)
  - CONTEXT containing the user's request, the action's arguments, and the date when available
  - A CRITERION describing what the value must satisfy

Decide binary PASS or FAIL strictly on the criterion. No partial credit. Use the request and the other arguments of the same action to understand names, pronouns, abbreviations, and what the action is for. Accept different wording that communicates the same required meaning. Do not require a message to repeat its recipient's name. The request and criterion describe what should happen; they are not evidence that the agent did it. Do not supply a missing answer from them or from a different action. Fail when the completed action omits, contradicts, or leaves unclear a required meaning. Output ONLY valid JSON in this shape:

{"passed": true, "reason": "a concise explanation naming the exact supporting text or the exact missing requirement"}

No prose, no markdown fences.

VALUE (as JSON):
"I dispute the $685 damage balance stated in your January 1, 2028 notice concerning our former Park Slope tenancy.

At the October 2024 post-handoff accounting, management confirmed that the full security deposit was returned, no cleaning, repair, damage, utility, key, or occupancy deductions were taken, and the former tenancy had a zero balance with no remaining condition claim. We returned possession and all keys on September 30, 2024, after the walkthrough.

Please withdraw this charge and confirm in writing that the account remains at $0 and that no collection or credit reporting action will be taken. If you contend the charge is still valid, send the complete itemized basis for it, including the inspection records, dated photographs, invoices or estimates, and the lease provision you rely on. Please also preserve all records related to the claim while it is disputed.

This dispute is not an acknowledgment of liability. Thank you,
Alex Valdez"

CONTEXT: {"user_request": "Find the inbox notice claiming a new balance or damage from our former Park Slope apartment and dispute it with the sender.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "send_email", "arguments": {"to": "claims@parkslopeproperty.com", "subject": "Dispute of $685 damage balance — former Park Slope tenancy", "body": "I dispute the $685 damage balance stated in your January 1, 2028 notice concerning our former Park Slope tenancy.

At the October 2024 post-handoff accounting, management confirmed that the full security deposit was returned, no cleaning, repair, damage, utility, key, or occupancy deductions were taken, and the former tenancy had a zero balance with no remaining condition claim. We returned possession and all keys on September 30, 2024, after the walkthrough.

Please withdraw this charge and confirm in writing that the account remains at $0 and that no collection or credit reporting action will be taken. If you contend the charge is still valid, send the complete itemized basis for it, including the inspection records, dated photographs, invoices or estimates, and the lease provision you rely on. Please also preserve all records related to the claim while it is disputed.

This dispute is not an acknowledgment of liability. Thank you,
Alex Valdez", "cc": null}, "field_being_checked": "result.body"}

CRITERION:
The reply says Alex and Devika received the full security deposit with no deductions and the tenancy had a zero balance with no remaining condition claim. It asks for written withdrawal of the new claim and does not offer payment or reopen the closeout.

Return the JSON verdict now.

{"passed":true,"reason":"The reply states that “the full security deposit was returned,” that no deductions were taken, and that “the former tenancy had a zero balance with no remaining condition claim.” It asks the sender to “withdraw this charge” and confirm the $0 balance in writing, without offering payment or reopening the closeout."}
